characters.name: Nyra Sol
characters.intro: Can I sit on that crate? My new shoes have taken the backs off both heels. A bandage apiece ought to do it.
characters.afterPurchase: I finished the shift in slippers. The boss took one look at my heels and went and got them himself.
characters.subsequentErrand: A couple of dressings for my bag. New girl starts tonight. Same shoes.
characters.flirt: You can have your crate back. I'd come in just for the company now.

characters.name: Celeste Vale
characters.intro: Anything I can eat in the wings? They moved my song up and my dinner's still on the stove.
characters.afterPurchase: Got through the song. Missed my entrance for the bows because I was finishing the last bite.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something pocket-sized. Crinkly wrapper's fine. I'll open it before the music.
characters.flirt: I saved you a seat with a good view of the exits. Best compliment I know.

characters.name: Mei Arden
characters.intro: Coffee for two, please. I booked both pianists. Same piano.
characters.afterPurchase: They played four hands. Now management thinks I did it on purpose.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee beans? I get to the booking desk before the kettle does.
characters.flirt: I'd put your name in my book. In pen, even.

characters.name: Rik Cale
characters.intro: See this tear? It's supposed to happen on the last chorus. I need cloth to patch it before the early show.
characters.afterPurchase: Held right through the encore. Now I have to work out how to tear it again.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any fabric I could put a knee through? On purpose this time.
characters.flirt: If you ever see the show, act surprised when the cuff goes.

characters.name: Vesper Nox
characters.intro: Small water. My room's right over the speakers. The glass on my bedside table walked off the edge.
characters.afterPurchase: A screw cap! My floor appreciates you.
characters.subsequentErrand: One with a lid, please. I knock things over when I'm half asleep.
characters.flirt: I like that you let me finish a sentence. Rare this close to closing time.

characters.name: Severin Ash
characters.intro: Shampoo, if you've got it. Two people want the same dressing room because the other sink smells.
characters.afterPurchase: It was the mop. I'd already made everybody wash their hair.
characters.subsequentErrand: Still doing the dressing-room order. We're down to the little bit you have to shake out.
characters.flirt: You've got a bit on your cheek. May I? There.

characters.name: Amara Dune
characters.intro: My flat's awfully quiet after a show. May I see the animals? Something I can carry home myself.
characters.afterPurchase: I've got company for breakfast now. We both like toast. Only one of us is allowed it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any animals in today? I've made room at home.
characters.flirt: You should hear me sing sometime when there's nobody talking over it.

characters.name: Tavon Blue
characters.intro: Two of us missed the meal break. The sheet says we took it. Funny how I'm still hungry.
characters.afterPurchase: I took the empty wrapper to payroll. Got the half hour put back.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any supper that doesn't need a pan? I'm buying for the late shift.
characters.flirt: You get a proper break today? I know a good step to sit on.

characters.name: Pippa Wren
characters.intro: A little torch? The cloakroom light's gone. I just handed a man his own hat as change.
characters.afterPurchase: Found three hats on one hook. No wonder everybody said theirs was missing.
characters.subsequentErrand: A torch for the desk. Ours keeps turning up in somebody's coat.
characters.flirt: I'd remember your coat without a ticket.

characters.name: Selene Cross
characters.intro: I need empty glass. Somebody put flowers in the carafes. Lovely until the ice comes round.
characters.afterPurchase: Left the flowers where they were. Water bottles on every table looked quite nice.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any empties? We get the deposit back if the crate goes out full.
characters.flirt: When I count heads for supper, I could count one more.

characters.name: Soren Vex
characters.intro: Could you pass me a water? I've been saying 'mind the step' since six.
characters.afterPurchase: The step finally got painted. I still say it. Can't seem to stop.
characters.subsequentErrand: Just water. It's a long walk back and I've done it once already.
characters.flirt: My brother's giving me that look. Means I've been chatting too long.

characters.name: Odette Sable
characters.intro: It's my turn to bring something sweet. There's a girl in the chorus who eats the corner off every piece.
characters.afterPurchase: She took the corners. I took the middle. We may have found a system.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something sweet for after the show. Pretty wrapping's wasted in our dressing room.
characters.flirt: I like your laugh. Easy to pick out from the stage.

characters.name: Zahara Flint
characters.intro: Have you a power cell? I'm back to doing bookings in pencil. I can't read my own fours.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the terminal on. My fours were fine. Somebody's been writing over them.
characters.subsequentErrand: Need a spare cell. I've got a whole wedding party under a single booking.
characters.flirt: You've made it into the appointment book under 'keep free'.

characters.name: Clemens Moss
characters.intro: Caught my cuff on a nail coming offstage. Do you have anything to wrap my wrist with?
characters.afterPurchase: It's closing up. The stage manager pulled the nail and gave it to me for luck.
characters.subsequentErrand: Little dressings? The stage kit's full of powder puffs.
characters.flirt: Talk into my good ear. I've still got the speakers in the other one.

characters.name: Ember Hale
characters.intro: The good news is the kitchen left me a fork. That's all the kitchen left me.
characters.afterPurchase: Had supper at the front desk. Nobody saw till I answered the bell with a mouthful.
characters.subsequentErrand: Noodles, if you've got them. I brought my fork.
characters.flirt: If you're ever walking my way, I wouldn't mind the company.

characters.name: Ilian Quill
characters.intro: There's glitter in my hairline. I stopped doing the glitter act six months ago. Shampoo?
characters.afterPurchase: Came off eventually. Funny seeing my own hair again.
characters.subsequentErrand: Another bottle of shampoo. My flatmate thinks the house buys it.
characters.flirt: You can tell me if my hair's still sparkling. I trust you.

characters.name: Melina Rose
characters.intro: Do the rats mind singing? That's a real question. The walls at my place are paper thin.
characters.afterPurchase: I've started rehearsing in the kitchen. The cage gets the quiet room.
characters.subsequentErrand: Can I have a look at the pets before I head in?
characters.flirt: The song about the shop? Didn't say WHICH shop, did I?

characters.name: Nyla Gold
characters.intro: Have you got coffee? I'm about to explain overtime to a man who gets paid for sleeping upstairs.
characters.afterPurchase: He read the sheet. Twice. The second time he found his glasses.
characters.subsequentErrand: Beans for the shift meeting. Last time we ran out before the vote.
characters.flirt: Sit in on our next meeting. I'll save you a cup.

characters.name: Juno Lace
characters.intro: The front desk has a drawer marked emergency. I looked. One button. I'd rather put some food in it.
characters.afterPurchase: Three people found that drawer on the first night. Nobody's found a use for the button.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something to tuck away till midnight. The button's still there.
characters.flirt: I catch myself listening for your bell even after I go home.

characters.name: Aurel Frost
characters.intro: How much for cloth? Our linen came back one tablecloth short and one enormous pair of curtains up.
characters.afterPurchase: Cut the curtains down. We've got tablecloths for months. Could do with actual napkins now.
characters.subsequentErrand: Plain cloth will do. Once the lights go down nobody can see the colour.
characters.flirt: Flowers on the table look nice. I'd bring you some if you wanted.

characters.name: Dara Wynn
characters.intro: My mother's coming to see where I work. She likes a hot drink before she asks difficult questions.
characters.afterPurchase: She stayed for both shows. Had plenty to say about the trombone player.
characters.subsequentErrand: Anything for the kettle? Mum's brought a friend this time.
characters.flirt: Mum asked who I keep popping out to see. What would you have told her?

characters.name: Floris Copper
characters.intro: A blister dressing. The blue pair fit fine standing still. Unfortunately I dance.
characters.afterPurchase: Wore the blue ones for the photographs and changed behind a curtain. Nobody noticed.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have a small bandage? Dress rehearsal.
characters.flirt: Come on a rehearsal night. You get the show and all the mistakes for free.

characters.name: Nerissa Bell
characters.intro: We're tying the reservation bell to the desk. People keep lifting it to see where the noise comes from.
characters.afterPurchase: It stayed put. Now they're lifting the deskcloth.
characters.subsequentErrand: A length of wire, please. I know exactly how long this time.
characters.flirt: There. An entire minute in my diary with your name on it.

characters.name: Kira Storm
characters.intro: Anything fruity to drink? Been pretending to sip from a prop glass all evening and now I'm thirsty.
characters.afterPurchase: Had to mark my bottle. Somebody put the real one back onstage.
characters.subsequentErrand: A fruit drink for the walk home. I'm off in ten minutes.
characters.flirt: I'd show you the trick if you'd promise to gasp at the right bit.

characters.name: Lio Bloom
characters.intro: Got food? My brother's waiting outside. He's finally old enough to pick me up after work, so he's doing it EVERY night.
characters.afterPurchase: He ate the lot on the way home. Said walking me back was hungry work.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something filling. My escort has hollow legs.
characters.flirt: Don't tell my brother, but I take the long way past here.

characters.name: Samira Moon
characters.intro: I need a flashlight for the stairs. We had a customer applaud the coat stand last night.
characters.afterPurchase: Lit the stairs. Same fellow said goodnight to the coat stand. I think he just likes it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Another light for the far landing. Those stairs do a funny turn halfway up.
characters.flirt: You're the one face I'd recognise on those stairs with the lights out.

characters.name: Isolde Ray
characters.intro: Water, room temperature if possible. My singing teacher can hear an ice cube from across the room.
characters.afterPurchase: Her first comment was that I'd finally been drinking water. Smug as anything, she was.
characters.subsequentErrand: Water for rehearsal. Got a lid that doesn't rattle?
characters.flirt: I could put your name in the second verse. Does it rhyme with anything?

characters.name: Yuna Crest
characters.intro: I'm making armbands for the floor crew. We tried badges. Can't see a badge in that light.
characters.afterPurchase: It worked. Even the owner asked me before he moved a table.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have any fabric left? Two new starters need bands.
characters.flirt: That colour suits you. Trust me, I've spent all week looking at fabric.

characters.name: Roel Silk
characters.intro: Coffee, please. Cloakroom tickets go from eighty-nine to ninety-eight. I've got to find eight coats before opening.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the missing tickets in my apron. Spent the whole night looking at everyone else's pockets.
characters.subsequentErrand: Is there coffee left? I haven't counted anything yet today.
characters.flirt: If I get the coat count right tonight, we're celebrating. You in?

characters.name: Iris Pearl
characters.intro: We're short of bottles for the water service. The florist swears ours arrived with her buckets.
characters.afterPurchase: She brought the bottles back full of carnations. I couldn't really ask her to empty them.
characters.subsequentErrand: Empty bottles? It's my night to lay the tables.
characters.flirt: There's one carnation going spare. Yours if you want it.

characters.name: Raven Tess
characters.intro: It's my birthday. Something sweet for one. If the house hears about it they'll make me stand on a chair.
characters.afterPurchase: Got all the way home before they sang at me. Over the phone, mercifully.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got something sweet? No candle needed.
characters.flirt: I like birthdays more when people remember them quietly. Like that.

characters.name: Ayana Reed
characters.intro: I fell asleep with the stage paint on. Look at the side of my face. That's the clean side.
characters.afterPurchase: My pillowcase may never recover. My face did, though.
characters.subsequentErrand: I need shampoo. The good wig's in for a wash.
characters.flirt: Tell me the song you like. I'll see if I know it.

characters.name: Bastiaan Solis
characters.intro: My appointment book has a gap the width of my thumb. Got something I can eat in that time?
characters.afterPurchase: Managed half before the bell. Half after. I'll take that.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something I can break in two and put away.
characters.flirt: I'd circle your name in my book. I'm usually very strict about the circles.

characters.name: Kaia Finch
characters.intro: Do you sell batteries? My hand mic went dead halfway through a joke. Nobody knows how it ends.
characters.afterPurchase: Told them the punchline. Honestly, it got a bigger laugh when the mic went dead.
characters.subsequentErrand: Spare cell for my mic. I'm trying new material.
characters.flirt: I had a line all ready for you. Much funnier in the mirror.

characters.name: Sable Venn
characters.intro: I can hear the rain coming through the ceiling in my room. Still haven't got drinking water, though.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the landlord upstairs with a bucket. Now it drips into his bucket instead of mine.
characters.subsequentErrand: Bottled water? Till somebody signs off on that pipe, I'm buying it here.
characters.flirt: You could come listen to the rain at mine. Great acoustics. One dry chair.

characters.name: Elodie Gray
characters.intro: Little bandage please. Paper cut. Four years on the floor and the rota finally gets me.
characters.afterPurchase: It stopped bleeding before I finished doing the rota. Left one lovely thumbprint on Friday.
characters.subsequentErrand: Need dressings for the office tin. Yes, the office gets one now.
characters.flirt: I'd shake your hand, but you know what happened to it.

characters.name: Mirei Thorn
characters.intro: Have you any beans? Our pianist plays a whole tone lower before he's had his first cup.
characters.afterPurchase: Same key, twice in a row. I bought him a mug that says 'keep it up'.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for the piano stool. I'll keep it off the keys this time.
characters.flirt: Don't laugh. I've actually rehearsed saying hello to you.

characters.name: Zola Fern
characters.intro: We're eating upstairs during the union count. Anything that only takes boiling water?
characters.afterPurchase: Lost by two votes. Had a second bowl and counted again. Still two.
characters.subsequentErrand: Noodles, please. We've another ballot to count.
characters.flirt: Fancy keeping me company at the count? You can have the chair that doesn't wobble.

characters.name: Coral Briar
characters.intro: Somebody's kid tore the velvet rope. I'd rather patch it before the boss sees. How much for cloth?
characters.afterPurchase: Patched it. Kid came back with his savings in a sock. I told him he owed me a drawing.
characters.subsequentErrand: Need fabric for the entrance rope. I'm getting rather good at this.
characters.flirt: I could put your name on the guest list. No queueing for you.

characters.name: Astra Lane
characters.intro: Hot sauce? The cook set aside a pot for staff. I think he forgot to put anything in it.
characters.afterPurchase: One drop was plenty. The drummer ignored me. We could hear him from the hall.
characters.subsequentErrand: A bit of seasoning for the staff pot. Drummer can bring his own.
characters.flirt: Want to try the staff supper some night? I'll serve the sauce separately.

characters.name: Lex Dawn
characters.intro: Last guest took my dinner by mistake. Left a glove. I'd get more use out of a sandwich.
characters.afterPurchase: He came back for the glove. He'd eaten the dinner. Brought me his wife's stew the next day.
characters.subsequentErrand: Anything ready to eat? I'll put my name on it.
characters.flirt: I'd share lunch with you. Deliberately, I mean.

characters.name: Jade Kest
characters.intro: Any cassettes? I've got a double tonight and I just heard the first act rehearsing my number.
characters.afterPurchase: She liked the new tune better than mine. We've swapped sets.
characters.subsequentErrand: Mind if I look through the tapes? I'm changing my set again.
characters.flirt: I've got a favourite tape. If I lent it to you, I'd have to come back.

characters.name: Althea Snow
characters.intro: Water for the queue outside. They think the line's moving because we've put the rope farther away.
characters.afterPurchase: Brought it out in cups. People started passing them down the line. That part worked.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm on the door again. Sealed water, whatever you've got.
characters.flirt: People are good at looking past the person on the door. You always say hello.

characters.name: Ruben Merrow
characters.intro: Do you sell screwdrivers? My trick box is stuck shut. It's much less of a trick this way.
characters.afterPurchase: Got it open at home. My spare key was inside. Brilliant place for it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Just a hand tool for the prop kit. Something I can lose on a dark stage.
characters.flirt: I'll do the trick at your counter one day if you've got a minute.

characters.name: Noemi Dusk
characters.intro: Something sweet. Somebody sent me flowers at work and I know exactly whose kid helped pick them.
characters.afterPurchase: He counted every sweet out loud. Took him longer to eat the first one than to give me the flowers.
characters.subsequentErrand: Seen any sweets a kid could carry without getting his cuffs sticky?
characters.flirt: I'd get flowers for you. I'd probably let the kid pick those too.

characters.name: Sandro Brass
characters.intro: Shampoo, please. The pump in the washroom gives you a handful of air and makes a terribly convincing noise.
characters.afterPurchase: Took the pump apart. Bet you've never seen so much hair round one spring.
characters.subsequentErrand: Washroom supplies again. At least the pump works.
characters.flirt: Nice talking to somebody who doesn't call me over with a whistle.

characters.name: Estelle Rook
characters.intro: I'm losing my voice. I've still got the low notes. Any coffee for the poor soul who's taking the high ones?
characters.afterPurchase: We split the song. Turned into a proper duet. I might keep it that way.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for two singers this morning.
characters.flirt: I'd like to hear what your speaking voice sounds like on a melody.

characters.name: Nika Azure
characters.intro: Someone put the first-aid tin on a shelf none of us can reach. Dressings, please. I'll keep these downstairs.
characters.afterPurchase: We moved the shelf. Manager had to ask me where the tin was. Very satisfying.
characters.subsequentErrand: A few dressings. The floor crew actually knows where to find them now.
characters.flirt: Hold still. Loose thread on your sleeve. There you go.

characters.name: Tal Reed
characters.intro: The bride asked for something fruity. She's the only one at the party nobody thought to get a drink for.
characters.afterPurchase: She sat behind reception for ten minutes and drank it in peace. Best part of the wedding, she said.
characters.subsequentErrand: A fruit drink for reception. I'd quite like to finish one myself.
characters.flirt: Ten minutes on the quiet side of reception? I know where they keep the spare key.

characters.name: Nia Cove
characters.intro: Got a power cell? The till drawer only opens when I hit the dance-floor lights.
characters.afterPurchase: Fixed. One elderly gentleman was rather disappointed. Thought the lights were for him.
characters.subsequentErrand: Till batteries, please. I'd like to close before sunrise for once.
characters.flirt: One of these nights I'll come by with nothing on the order sheet.

characters.name: Vivienne Carrow
characters.intro: Could I buy a torch? The gallery portrait looks fine until somebody turns off the skylight.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the problem. Varnish on one cheek, none on the other. Much cheaper than buying another portrait.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like a light I can take down to the storeroom.

characters.name: Marisol Vane
characters.intro: Coffee for my salon. Last week the guests stayed five hours and agreed on nothing except that the coffee was awful.
characters.afterPurchase: They've asked for the same coffee next week. First unanimous decision we've had.
characters.subsequentErrand: The salon's up to nine people. I'd better get more beans.

characters.name: Ophelia Crest
characters.intro: Do you have fabric I can take with me? The mill sent a swatch smaller than the moth hole I'm matching.
characters.afterPurchase: Pretty good match in daylight. Under the stairs it looks perfect. That's where the coat lives.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'll buy cloth by the piece. I've brought the coat this time.

characters.name: Lenora Chase
characters.intro: A screwdriver, please. My father left me his shipping desk. Somebody painted the cash drawer shut.
characters.afterPurchase: There was one coin in it. I'd have paid ten times that to hear him explain the paint.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something for the desk's hinges. I'm doing this drawer by drawer.

characters.name: Amelie Korr
characters.intro: Do you carry perfume? I've spent all morning smelling sample cards and I can't tell any two apart.
characters.afterPurchase: Tried it outdoors. Reminded me of my aunt's hallway. I kept it.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like to see your perfume. Please leave the bottle closed till I decide.

characters.name: Daphne Welles
characters.intro: A cassette for the car home. Live music all evening and the only tune in my head is the lift bell.
characters.afterPurchase: I was still listening when we got home. Made the driver go round the block.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have any tapes? My driver gets first pick this time.

characters.name: Rosalind Veil
characters.intro: I'm seating the two uncles at opposite tables. I need something festive they can both drink.
characters.afterPurchase: One raised his glass across the room. The other raised his. Nobody got up. A triumph.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something fruity for the next toast, if you have it.

characters.name: Octavia Senn
characters.intro: We've twelve rooms and by some miracle every last bottle of shampoo ran out on the same morning.
characters.afterPurchase: Found a whole crate behind the guest towels. I didn't tell the guests.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm doing the washroom order myself. May I see your shampoo?

characters.name: Akemi Ward
characters.intro: A magnifier? Somebody claims this print is signed. At my age every speck looks like a signature.
characters.afterPurchase: It said 'turn over'. On the back was the signature. You may laugh.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have you any magnifying glasses? My assistant keeps borrowing mine.

characters.name: Eveline Shaw
characters.intro: Do you sell lottery tickets? My club has barred us from playing cards till someone returns the dining table.
characters.afterPurchase: Nobody won. Tremendously civil evening. We got the table back.
characters.subsequentErrand: A ticket for the club draw. Just a little one.

characters.name: Cressida Thorn
characters.intro: Beans, please. Yes, I import tea. My sister won't drink the stuff.
characters.afterPurchase: Served it to her in my best teapot. She asked for a second cup.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for my sister's visit. I've given up converting her.

characters.name: Paloma Greer
characters.intro: The theatre lost its interval music. You can hear a hundred people trying to unwrap mints quietly. Any tapes?
characters.afterPurchase: We played the tape. Now they unwrap their mints in time.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm looking for a cassette for the foyer.

characters.name: Henrietta Moss
characters.intro: Some wire for a clasp. The customer wants it secure enough to dance in and loose enough to throw at her husband.
characters.afterPurchase: She danced. Kept the necklace on. Good enough for me.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got fine wire? I'll know if it'll bend when I see it.

characters.name: Delphine Raye
characters.intro: Bandages for the foundation cupboard. Our letterhead cost more than everything in it.
characters.afterPurchase: The nurse opened the cupboard and used them in front of the board. We're budgeting for stock now.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings again. This time I've got a purchase order.

characters.name: Lucienne Bell
characters.intro: May I buy that empty bottle? My grandmother kept buttons in one exactly like it.
characters.afterPurchase: It fits her old stopper. I've started on the buttons.
characters.subsequentErrand: I collect empty glass. Little variations in the neck, mostly.

characters.name: Misaki Voss
characters.intro: I need shampoo for the hotel. Someone filled the dispensers with furniture polish. The floor smells gorgeous.
characters.afterPurchase: We caught it before check-in. I've put a shelf between those two crates.
characters.subsequentErrand: Another washroom order. I'll read the label myself, thank you.

characters.name: Camille Dorne
characters.intro: My favourite restaurant changed cooks. I'm trying to place what's missing in the sauce. Any seasoning?
characters.afterPurchase: Turns out he'd left it mild for me. Rather mortifying. I took him the bottle.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something spicy for lunch. The chef's stopped taking it personally.

characters.name: Beatrix Cole
characters.intro: Fabric, please. My client approved the curtain design by sitting on the sample. I need that sample back.
characters.afterPurchase: I made a cushion from the piece I bought here. Now she's ordered cushions. Still no curtains.
characters.subsequentErrand: May I look at the cloth? We're finally discussing the windows.

characters.name: Safiya Noor
characters.intro: I'd like drinking water for a caravan driver. He waited through my entire meeting in the sun.
characters.afterPurchase: He's made me write the water stop into the contract. Quite right too.
characters.subsequentErrand: Sealed water for the road. The drivers sign for it themselves now.

characters.name: Florence Quay
characters.intro: I used to keep orchids in that heated room. It's a nursery now. Do you have a live animal I could take home?
characters.afterPurchase: My gardener still asks when I'm putting the orchids back. He's the one who named the newcomer.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm here for the animals. May I see what you've raised?

characters.name: Greer “Bulkhead” Voss
characters.intro: Three porters on the roof. I'm taking their water up before somebody decides to be brave about it.
characters.afterPurchase: They came down for a proper break today. Took the bottles up empty just to prove a point.
characters.subsequentErrand: What have you got in drinking water? I've got a free hand on the way back.

characters.name: Sigrid “Floodwall” Renn
characters.intro: Do you have a flashlight? There's something in the intake grille. From up here it looks a lot like a hand.
characters.afterPurchase: Work glove. Still spent half an hour asking around to make sure its owner had both hands.
characters.subsequentErrand: I could use a light for the dive bag. The little ones go missing.

characters.name: Tesa Morrow
characters.intro: A filter, please. I promised the tenants I'd bring the old one to the meeting. You should see it.
characters.afterPurchase: I passed the old filter round in a saucer. Nobody argued about the maintenance levy after that.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any filters in stock? There's a date pencilled on mine and today's the date.

characters.name: Anika Rook
characters.intro: The convoy's leaving early. I need something I can eat standing up.
characters.afterPurchase: Ate by the barrier, with the engine running. Best five minutes of the trip.
characters.subsequentErrand: We've a short halt. What can I eat here?

characters.name: Branna Kest
characters.intro: Can you open the first-aid shelf? Got a wire end under my thumbnail. Yes, I was wearing gloves.
characters.afterPurchase: Finger's fine. Got the glove pinned up in the shed. Hole goes clean through it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings for the crane cab. It's a long climb with a cut finger.

characters.name: Dalia Sorn
characters.intro: I'm buying break food. If I ask all twelve what they want, we'll miss the break.
characters.afterPurchase: Put the snacks in a bowl. They sorted the shares before I'd taken my coat off.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something I can divide among a crew, please.

characters.name: Captain Iona Rusk
characters.intro: We sail when the tea-coloured fog lifts. Until then I'd rather have actual coffee.
characters.afterPurchase: The lookout could smell the pot from the bow. I had six extra people on watch.
characters.subsequentErrand: Beans. We've a night sailing.

characters.name: Tarek “Knots” Vale
characters.intro: Got pistol rounds? I'm doing the count myself. The last quartermaster counted the rattles.
characters.afterPurchase: Two boxes rattled. One contained a loose screw. I've changed the tally.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying ammunition. I check every box before it goes aboard.

characters.name: Nell Vek
characters.intro: A screwdriver with a handle left on it. The one in the hatch is staying there till the door opens.
characters.afterPurchase: Door's open. Found two more screwdrivers on the far side. Probably mine too.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm pricing hand tools for the gangway locker.

characters.name: Felix “Undertow” Dane
characters.intro: A light for my chart. I missed a buoy last night and spent an hour navigating by the smell of a bakery.
characters.afterPurchase: Same bend was easy with the chart lit. Bakery was closed. We'd have been in trouble.
characters.subsequentErrand: Show me a torch I can keep by the wheel.

characters.name: Asha Marr
characters.intro: My crew will eat anything if it stings their tongue. What've you got for the stew?
characters.afterPurchase: The skipper asked what cut of meat I'd used. Lentils. I said I'd tell her next voyage.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm cooking for twelve. Just the seasoning today.

characters.name: Bram Sile
characters.intro: The cargo scale died with a crate on it. Can I get a cell before the ice melts?
characters.afterPurchase: Weighed it with about a cup less ice. Nobody fancied arguing over a cup.
characters.subsequentErrand: A battery. I can put the scale down if you need the counter.

characters.name: Rhea Cinder
characters.intro: I need a weapon for the boarding locker. The last one went over with a coat hooked on it.
characters.afterPurchase: Had the locker moved away from the coat hooks. Should've done it before.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm checking the arms shelf. Fleet money, so I need a receipt.

characters.name: Captain Sabine Marrow
characters.intro: Some wire. There's a brass nameplate under the wreck and I'd like to bring it up whole.
characters.afterPurchase: Her name was Ada. Lettering came up under my thumb. I've given the plate to her old mate.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm after salvage wire. A short bit's useful too.

characters.name: Kestrel Marr
characters.intro: Ammunition for the flare watch. We stow the live rounds separately. You'd think that went without saying.
characters.afterPurchase: Made two lockers. Painted one lid red. Made the new hand explain which was which.
characters.subsequentErrand: Pistol rounds for the ship's manifest, please.

characters.name: Lark Sable
characters.intro: I need power for the signal lamp. Can you imagine running the whole length of the jetty to say 'wait'?
characters.afterPurchase: Lit the lamp. Other end flashed back for the first time in a week.
characters.subsequentErrand: Spare cells for the night signal.

characters.name: Sister Elian Reed
characters.intro: We've somebody at the relief house who's too shy to join the queue. I'll buy food and sit with him.
characters.afterPurchase: He ate when I stopped asking questions. Next day he sat beside somebody else.
characters.subsequentErrand: Is there a meal I can take with me? It's for the quiet table.

characters.name: Brother Oren Pike
characters.intro: Something for a water filter. I found tadpoles in the cistern. The children would like me to leave them.
characters.afterPurchase: Moved them to a bucket first. Got six small inspectors checking that bucket daily.
characters.subsequentErrand: A spare filter, if you have one. The cistern's open this week.

characters.name: Deacon Sana Ves
characters.intro: I need a clean cylinder. I've two water samples and I've dropped the lid into one of them.
characters.afterPurchase: Ran the tests again. The lid was the only suspect thing in either sample.
characters.subsequentErrand: Measuring glass? Graduations I can read from above would be nice.

characters.name: Lev Anwen
characters.intro: Bottled water for the road. My route's got a drinking fountain on the map and a square of dry cement in person.
characters.afterPurchase: I marked the map. Found three more couriers drinking from their own bottles there.
characters.subsequentErrand: What can I get in a sealed bottle? I've a delivery past the last tap.

characters.name: Mother Maelin Tor
characters.intro: Could I buy a magnifier? Someone wrote the donor's name so small we've credited three different people.
characters.afterPurchase: It was a family name, all one word. I sent the family a clean copy.
characters.subsequentErrand: Magnifying glass for the archive. We do more reading than anyone budgets for.

characters.name: Ivar Renn
characters.intro: Noodles? My lunch guest doesn't like the relief-house soup. I make the soup. Trying not to take it personally.
characters.afterPurchase: He ate a whole bowl. His new teeth can't manage the lumps. I'd never have guessed.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something soft I can make with a kettle.

characters.name: Ren Calder
characters.intro: Meeting at six. Coffee first. I refuse to take a strike vote on an empty pot.
characters.afterPurchase: We went through the pot before the minutes had been read. Passed the motion though.
characters.subsequentErrand: Union's buying the beans today. I'll keep the receipt.

characters.name: Mika Toren
characters.intro: Have you a hand tool I can lend out? Last apprentice used my best screwdriver to open a tin.
characters.afterPurchase: Bought him a tin opener with his first overtime. My drivers have had a quiet week.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm off the Engineering counter. Shopping for my own toolbox today.

characters.name: Gus Holl
characters.intro: Have you a battery for a lamp? The little red one on my belt's getting dimmer every time I look at it.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the fuse by its light. Spent longer finding where I'd laid the cover down.
characters.subsequentErrand: A spare cell. I swap them before the night shift.

characters.name: Nadi Senn
characters.intro: I need a piece of electronics I can take apart. My line's counting an empty belt as twelve cans.
characters.afterPurchase: Bad contact. Shook it and got thirteen. I've kept it to show the trainees.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any electronic parts? I can use them even if the casing's cracked.

characters.name: Pavel Quill
characters.intro: Something I can eat with one hand. There's a stop cord on my left and they told me to stay put.
characters.afterPurchase: Got my break. First time in a month the line jammed while the foreman was watching it.
characters.subsequentErrand: A wrapped snack. Oil gets everywhere on that line.

characters.name: Elsa Vann
characters.intro: I'm looking for a lamp. Dispatch put the midnight shelf below a window. Excellent at noon.
characters.afterPurchase: Moved the midnight labels. Now the morning crew keep asking who tidied up.
characters.subsequentErrand: A torch I can take down between the stacks.

characters.name: Jessa “Goggles” Flint
characters.intro: Need wire. My bike basket has one joint left and I'm still carrying the other three in it.
characters.afterPurchase: Basket held. Lost the bell instead. You can't have everything.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any wire? I've a bike outside with opinions.

characters.name: Iman Raye
characters.intro: Is there a filter on that shelf? Somebody stuffed a rag in the pump. It was my rag. There's my name on it.
characters.afterPurchase: The water's clear. I washed the rag and the name came off immediately.
characters.subsequentErrand: Pump filter, please. I brought the dimensions.

characters.name: Dr. Ada Miren
characters.intro: I need dressings for the waiting room. A kid walked through the clinic door, saw the queue and walked straight back out.
characters.afterPurchase: Caught him on the steps. Let him put the dressing on himself. He came in the next time.
characters.subsequentErrand: Small dressings for reception. People ask there first.

characters.name: Jonah Fenn
characters.intro: Bandages. The bag's empty. Sorry, I'm counting in my head.
characters.afterPurchase: Went back to the call with a full bag. I've slept since then, in case you were wondering.
characters.subsequentErrand: Can I see what you've got for wounds?

characters.name: Priya Kade
characters.intro: Small bottle, please. My rounds include three flights with a sign that says 'lift tomorrow'.
characters.afterPurchase: Somebody crossed out tomorrow and wrote Thursday. Didn't say which one.
characters.subsequentErrand: Water for my delivery round. Nothing I need two hands to open.

characters.name: Emil Roth
characters.intro: If you've got a screwdriver, I'd like one. A tray rattles when the sterilizer heats up. Makes everyone duck.
characters.afterPurchase: One screw loose. Whole room stood there watching me turn it. Nice round of applause.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any hand tools for the clinic workshop?

characters.name: Lina Voss
characters.intro: Anything fresh? I'm doing a tasting for people who think they hate vegetables. Starting small.
characters.afterPurchase: One woman asked to take the stalks home. Nobody ever asks for the stalks.
characters.subsequentErrand: A little produce for the class. I'll see what's ripe.

characters.name: Tomas Wren
characters.intro: Power cell for my stretcher lamp. Carrying someone down dark stairs is quite enough work without guessing the steps.
characters.afterPurchase: The patient counted the stairs out loud for me. Made it easier on both of us.
characters.subsequentErrand: A cell for the ambulance, please.

characters.name: Verena Doss
characters.intro: You carry seasoning? I'm away from the Cannery today. I want to see what everyone else puts in their soup.
characters.afterPurchase: Took a spoonful to our cook. He went quiet and put some in his pocket. From him that's high praise.
characters.subsequentErrand: I've come to buy spices. I'll take them back to the Co-op myself.

characters.name: Silas Nemm
characters.intro: Empty glass for a class. I've got a dozen examples of bad seams and nothing to show a good one.
characters.afterPurchase: They spotted the good bottle right off. Then one pointed out a crack I'd missed in the bad pile.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'll buy empty glass. May I turn it against the light?

characters.name: Zuri Vell
characters.intro: I'm working the Depot till morning. Can I get some coffee before I go in?
characters.afterPurchase: Drank it on the loading step. Ten quiet minutes with the shutters down. Lovely.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for the early deliveries. My own money today.

characters.name: Oswin Rell
characters.intro: Got any soda? My dad used to keep his favourites under the sink like they were the family jewels.
characters.afterPurchase: He recognised the flavour with his eyes closed. Couldn't remember the name. Neither could I.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm looking for soda we can taste at home.

characters.name: Kiara Mott
characters.intro: A driver for the Glassmarket shelves. The left one's started leaning and so have all the goods on it.
characters.afterPurchase: Level now. I've got so used to reaching downhill I keep missing the till.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any hand tools? I'm fixing the stall on my day off.

characters.name: Dev Sorn
characters.intro: I need a glass for reading freight seals. Yesterday I signed for eight drums of something beginning with S.
characters.afterPurchase: Soap. A relief to everybody, especially the man who thought he'd sent spirits.
characters.subsequentErrand: A magnifier. The new freight marks are even smaller.

characters.name: Una Fen
characters.intro: I need food for the rats I'm taking to market. Sold the feed tin along with the cage, didn't I?
characters.afterPurchase: They ate before the trip. The buyer asked why they were all asleep.
characters.subsequentErrand: Animal feed, please. Got to keep the sale stock fed.

characters.appearance: woman age 36, warm brown skin, wide nose, dark coiled hair tied high, calm direct expression
characters.name: Avery Stillwell
characters.intro: I've got a water gauge that only lights up if you slap it. I'm going to try a new battery before I break my hand.
characters.afterPurchase: New cell, no slapping. Had to go down and tell the other keeper. He was still hitting it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got a cell to fit the night gauge?

characters.appearance: man age 52, tan skin, broad face, receding gray hair, trimmed mustache, tired gentle eyes
characters.name: Gideon Ashford
characters.intro: Something for the soup, please. There's a queue forming and all I've got in the pot so far is good intentions and onions.
characters.afterPurchase: The onions caught on the bottom. Everybody asked for the recipe anyway.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying seasoning for the relief kitchen.

characters.appearance: woman age 44, olive skin, angular nose, black bob with one silver streak, reserved expression
characters.name: Morgan Morrow
characters.intro: I visit people at home. I'd rather bring my own water than make somebody ashamed of an empty kettle.
characters.afterPurchase: Had a drink with a man who hasn't had company in weeks. We mostly watched his kettle cool.
characters.subsequentErrand: A bottle for the visiting bag. Small will do.

characters.appearance: man age 29, dark skin, narrow jaw, cropped curls, slight crooked smile
characters.name: Ellis Venn
characters.intro: Wash supplies? Somebody polished the shrine with hair oil. The whole place smells like my grandfather.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the last oily handprint off the rail. Left one under the ledge. I quite like the smell.
characters.subsequentErrand: Shampoo, if there's any. My hair gets the shrine dust too.

characters.appearance: woman age 61, pale skin, lined face, short white hair and rectangular spectacles
characters.name: Quinn Tallis
characters.intro: A torch for the record room. The names on the bottom shelf get lost in the shadow of my head.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the date they needed. It was written in the margin next to a grocery list.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like a portable light for reading the low shelves.

characters.appearance: woman age 32, dark brown skin, oval face, side braid and small scar at eyebrow
characters.name: Riley Fenwick
characters.intro: Something for the road. I said I could walk the route fasting. That was yesterday, sitting down.
characters.afterPurchase: I made it to the spring. Had lunch halfway. Nobody up there asked.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have any snacks that travel well?

characters.appearance: man age 67, pale weathered skin, broad nose, bald crown and gray side hair, deep smile lines
characters.name: Arden Brass
characters.intro: I'm checking a batch of filters. Need one from a different supplier to see which of us is making the mistake.
characters.afterPurchase: It was our measuring jug. Somebody had drawn the fill line on with a pencil.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like another filter from ordinary stock.

characters.appearance: woman age 48, tawny skin, stocky build, dark auburn crop, practical serious expression
characters.name: Sage Corven
characters.intro: Any seeds for the garden by the steps? The children saved a whole bed for something you can actually eat.
characters.afterPurchase: They wrote their names on sticks and planted those first. At least the rows are straight.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like seed stock. We've another bit of ground by the rail.

characters.appearance: man age 41, olive skin, hooked nose, wavy black hair, light stubble, relaxed shoulders
characters.name: Robin Lowell
characters.intro: A bottle for the tithe desk. It's hard asking people to share their water while you're drinking theirs.
characters.afterPurchase: An old woman made me take my bottle home full. Insisted I try hers. I did.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'll buy my own water for the collection round.

characters.appearance: woman age 27, freckled light skin, red hair in loose bun, wide-set modest-sized eyes
characters.name: Emery Hale
characters.intro: Do you sell cloth? We're dividing the hall for overnight beds. People need somewhere to change.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the screen up. First thing somebody did behind it was have a good cry in private.
characters.subsequentErrand: More fabric for the hall, please.

characters.appearance: woman age 55, dark skin, silver twists, round strong face, skeptical eyebrow
characters.name: Alex Darrow
characters.intro: I watch the spring after closing. A torch would save me explaining to every late pilgrim why I'm standing in the dark.
characters.afterPurchase: A father came down with his kid to look for frogs. Glad I saw what he was carrying before I yelled.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something for the night watch. Just a light today.

characters.appearance: man age 35, brown skin, tall forehead, short dark curls, compact beard, watchful eyes
characters.name: Reese Evers
characters.intro: I need an empty bottle for the ceremony. Somebody took the silver jug home to clean and forgot where they live, apparently.
characters.afterPurchase: Used the glass. You could see the water passing from hand to hand. They want to keep it that way.
characters.subsequentErrand: Clean empty glass for the spring room.

characters.appearance: woman age 38, pale skin, long narrow face, dark braid around crown, calm gaze
characters.name: Cameron Rill
characters.intro: A measuring cylinder. Our well sample arrived in an old pickle jar. Smells exactly as you'd expect.
characters.afterPurchase: New sample passed. Took me a while to convince the committee it was the jar that had failed.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying lab glass for well inspections.

characters.appearance: man age 59, olive skin, graying ponytail, rugged cheeks, full salt-and-pepper beard
characters.name: Skyler Keene
characters.intro: A family asked if they could have coffee after the service. I know where to find flowers at this hour. Coffee's harder.
characters.afterPurchase: We sat until the pot was cold. Somebody started telling stories about her and nobody wanted to leave.
characters.subsequentErrand: Beans for the chapel kitchen. I keep a pot there now.

characters.appearance: woman age 30, deep brown skin, shaved sides and swept curls, confident expression
characters.name: Finley Flint
characters.intro: I missed a door on the meal round. Got the empty carrier to prove it. Can I buy a dinner?
characters.afterPurchase: The man at number six took it and gave me two empty dishes. Seems I'd missed him before.
characters.subsequentErrand: Anything ready to eat? I keep one extra on my round.

characters.appearance: woman age 64, tan skin, narrow eyes, loose gray bun, visible age lines
characters.name: Jules Rowe
characters.intro: Soft cloth for wrapping a register. The spine's coming away. I can carry the book or all the pages separately.
characters.afterPurchase: Carried it flat. There was a pressed flower in the middle. The archivist knew who'd left it.
characters.subsequentErrand: A piece of fabric for an old book.

characters.appearance: man age 46, pale skin, blond receding hair, sturdy jaw, clean shaven
characters.name: Blair Merrick
characters.intro: I'm meant to bless the pump tomorrow. I'd like a screwdriver. That rattle's loud enough to drown out a blessing.
characters.afterPurchase: Tightened the cover before the ceremony. Heard every word. So did the neighbours.
characters.subsequentErrand: What hand tools do you have? They keep inviting me back.

characters.appearance: woman age 42, olive skin, wide cheekbones, short plum-brown curls, small spectacles
characters.name: Drew Strand
characters.intro: My class is keeping a seed diary. So far it's a diary about an empty tray. Can you help?
characters.afterPurchase: First shoot came up on a Sunday. Whole class accused me of putting it there.
characters.subsequentErrand: Seeds for the school windowsill, please.

characters.appearance: man age 28, dark skin, broad jaw, flat top hair, friendly expression
characters.name: Casey Ames
characters.intro: Have you a bandage? My pilgrims turn up with new boots every time. I can usually tell who'll need it first.
characters.afterPurchase: The one in the oldest boots got the blister. So much for my professional judgment.
characters.subsequentErrand: I carry wound dressings for the walking route.

characters.appearance: woman age 50, freckled tan skin, wavy chestnut hair with gray temples, steady eyes
characters.name: Taylor Calder
characters.intro: Do you have any empty glass? The rain off each roof tastes different. I'd like to find out if that's just me.
characters.afterPurchase: Did a blind tasting. My favourite roof turned out to be my neighbour's tap. He'd been helping.
characters.subsequentErrand: Empty bottles, please. I've got another roof to try.

characters.appearance: woman age 29, dark skin, narrow jaw, cropped curls, slight crooked smile
characters.name: Zara Venn
characters.intro: No tap in the crane cab. Once I climb up, that's my morning. Can I get a bottle?
characters.afterPurchase: From up there I could see the water queue curl all the way round your corner.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something to drink up in the cab, please.

characters.appearance: woman age 61, pale skin, lined face, short white hair and rectangular spectacles
characters.name: Ingrid Tallis
characters.intro: Bundle came in with the straps cut. I'm going to tie it up before the night gang get blamed. Wire?
characters.afterPurchase: Driver came back looking for his wire cutters. We had a useful little talk.
characters.subsequentErrand: Wire for the freight shed. Leave it coiled if you can.

characters.appearance: woman age 32, dark brown skin, oval face, side braid and small scar at eyebrow
characters.name: Nadia Fenwick
characters.intro: Scraped my ankle on a sunken ladder. Need it dressed before I pull the suit back on.
characters.afterPurchase: Went back down in daylight. That ladder was the only bit of the boat still bolted on straight.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings for the dive bag.

characters.appearance: woman age 67, pale weathered skin, broad nose, bald crown and gray side hair, deep smile lines
characters.name: Freya Brass
characters.intro: There's a gap between the ferry and the pier nobody sees at night. I want a torch on it.
characters.afterPurchase: A pram wheel caught there. We had it out before the mother even let go of the handle.
characters.subsequentErrand: Buying a light for the ferry rail.

characters.appearance: woman age 48, tawny skin, stocky build, dark auburn crop, practical serious expression
characters.name: Elara Corven
characters.intro: I'm coming back with the same load I took out. One family said the water tasted of rubber. Got a filter?
characters.afterPurchase: Turned out to be a new hose. I drank the first cup at every stop after that.
characters.subsequentErrand: Water filter. If it saves me a second trip it'll pay for itself.

characters.appearance: woman age 41, olive skin, hooked nose, wavy black hair, defined jaw, relaxed shoulders
characters.name: Astrid Lowell
characters.intro: Something I can eat before the next barge. Hang on, that's its horn, isn't it?
characters.afterPurchase: They were still arguing about the berth when I got there. I could've sat down for lunch.
characters.subsequentErrand: Wrapped food. I've got to be back when that horn goes.

characters.appearance: woman age 27, freckled light skin, red hair in loose bun, wide-set modest-sized eyes
characters.name: Sonia Hale
characters.intro: Have you a magnifier? They want my mark on a weld and I can't see the edge cleanly.
characters.afterPurchase: Found a hairline crack. Foreman crossed my name off the job and sent it back. Fine by me.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'd like a glass for checking small welds.

characters.appearance: woman age 55, dark skin, silver twists, round strong face, skeptical eyebrow
characters.name: Helga Darrow
characters.intro: Can I see the handle on that one? My left hand doesn't close properly. The thin grips are no good to me.
characters.afterPurchase: Took the lid off on my own. Sounds like nothing. First time since the press caught me.
characters.subsequentErrand: You had some decent tools here last time. Mind if I try the grip?

characters.appearance: woman age 35, brown skin, tall forehead, short dark curls, strong cheekbones, watchful eyes
characters.name: Runa Evers
characters.intro: Bandages. I got impatient with a hatch. Hatch won.
characters.afterPurchase: It's the hand I sign with. The apprentice had to fill out the accident report. Very neat writing.
characters.subsequentErrand: Wound dressings for the breaking yard.

characters.appearance: woman age 38, pale skin, long narrow face, dark braid around crown, calm gaze
characters.name: Maelle Rill
characters.intro: That floodgate counter's stopped at ninety-nine. I'll try a fresh cell before I send a man into the pit.
characters.afterPurchase: Counter rolled over to a hundred. We all stood there and watched it. Been waiting years for that.
characters.subsequentErrand: Spare cell for the gate counter.

characters.appearance: woman age 59, olive skin, graying ponytail, rugged cheeks, short salt-and-pepper hair
characters.name: Inga Keene
characters.intro: I need dry cloth. We got the boy out of the canal. Now he's sitting there blue as my apron.
characters.afterPurchase: He came in to give the towel back. His mum made him wash it first.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any cloth for drying people off? The boat locker's nearly empty.

characters.appearance: woman age 30, deep brown skin, shaved sides and swept curls, confident expression
characters.name: Tova Flint
characters.intro: Coffee beans, please. Three of us are on the moorings tonight.
characters.afterPurchase: There were only two of us in the end. Dav's home with his little girl. We kept his share.
characters.subsequentErrand: Whatever coffee you've got. The tug leaves in ten minutes.

characters.appearance: woman age 64, tan skin, narrow eyes, loose gray bun, visible age lines
characters.name: Brienne Rowe
characters.intro: Wire. I lowered a plumb bob into the pump shaft. The string's come back without it.
characters.afterPurchase: Hooked it back out. Also found a wedding ring. Somebody on shift owes me a drink.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have any wire for a rigging job?

characters.appearance: woman age 46, pale skin, blond receding hair, sturdy jaw, weathered features
characters.name: Hilda Merrick
characters.intro: A hand tool for my daughter. She's starting at the docks. Don't show me your prettiest one. Show me one that lasts.
characters.afterPurchase: She put her initials in the handle before she'd even taken her coat off.
characters.subsequentErrand: Looking at tools. It's the apprentice who gets to choose this time.

characters.appearance: woman age 42, olive skin, wide cheekbones, short plum-brown curls, small spectacles
characters.name: Solveig Strand
characters.intro: Something to drink at the rail siding? There's a tea hut marked on the timetable. There hasn't been one for ten years.
characters.afterPurchase: The porter remembered the hut. Said the tea was terrible. Felt better about missing it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Water for the siding, please.

characters.appearance: woman age 28, dark skin, broad jaw, flat top hair, friendly expression
characters.name: Greta Ames
characters.intro: I'm buying a light for the tow. Almost took two boats last night. Couldn't see where the second rope went.
characters.afterPurchase: Saw the spare rope before we pulled. My mate hasn't mentioned my eyesight all morning.
characters.subsequentErrand: A torch for checking towlines.

characters.appearance: woman age 50, freckled tan skin, wavy chestnut hair with gray temples, steady eyes
characters.name: Leona Calder
characters.intro: I need a clean cylinder. Ballast samples got mixed up. Both jars say starboard.
characters.afterPurchase: Marked the new one on the glass itself. There's only so many ways to spell starboard wrong.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any measuring glass I can put in a padded case?

characters.appearance: woman age 36, warm brown skin, wide nose, dark coiled hair tied high, calm direct expression
characters.name: Svetla Stillwell
characters.intro: First day aloft. Do you know anything good to eat if you're a bit nervous? I'll settle for a snack.
characters.afterPurchase: Was fine once we started lifting. My lunch stayed where I put it, too.
characters.subsequentErrand: I've a crane shift. Can I see the snacks?

characters.appearance: woman age 52, tan skin, broad face, receding gray hair, strong brows, tired gentle eyes
characters.name: Dagny Ashford
characters.intro: Fabric to lay over a wet patch. I've got half the harbour leaning over my shoulder trying to tell me where it leaks.
characters.afterPurchase: Saw the first damp spot right through the cloth. Fixed that one and the crowd went away.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any cloth for a hull job?

characters.appearance: woman age 44, olive skin, angular nose, black bob with one silver streak, reserved expression
characters.name: Daria Morrow
characters.intro: The lift whistle runs on a cell. Yesterday I had to yell. Today I sound like this. Can you sell me one?
characters.afterPurchase: The whistle's working. Had to tell the crew twice it was me blowing it.
characters.subsequentErrand: A cell for the lift signals.

characters.appearance: man age 67, pale weathered skin, broad nose, bald crown and gray side hair, deep smile lines
characters.name: Hector Brass
characters.intro: Need a screwdriver narrow enough to get past my knuckles. Got a pipe boxed into a corner.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the cover off. Plenty of room inside. It's the person outside they forgot about.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have any hand tools I can take a look at?

characters.appearance: woman age 48, tawny skin, stocky build, dark auburn crop, practical serious expression
characters.name: Agnes Corven
characters.intro: Filter for a pump, please. The spare hanging on the wall is the one we took off last winter.
characters.afterPurchase: Wrote USED across the old one. Should see the size of the letters.
characters.subsequentErrand: What filters are you carrying today?

characters.appearance: man age 41, olive skin, hooked nose, wavy black hair, light stubble, relaxed shoulders
characters.name: Duncan Lowell
characters.intro: I've got two crews in a room who won't talk to each other. Lunch first, I think.
characters.afterPurchase: Passed the food round and discovered they were both angry about the same missing payslip.
characters.subsequentErrand: A meal for the union office. We may be there a while.

characters.appearance: woman age 27, freckled light skin, red hair in loose bun, wide-set modest-sized eyes
characters.name: Wren Hale
characters.intro: Coffee beans? I get home just as everybody else gets up. Would be nice to share breakfast for once.
characters.afterPurchase: Stayed awake till my kid went to school. Took my work boots off at the gate to sneak back in.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for breakfast. Yes, I know what time it is.

characters.appearance: woman age 55, dark skin, silver twists, round strong face, skeptical eyebrow
characters.name: Fern Darrow
characters.intro: Need a torch. Someone's built a cupboard round the meter and filled it with shoes.
characters.afterPurchase: Twenty-three pairs. The lady counted them coming out and going back. Meter took a minute.
characters.subsequentErrand: Buying a light for the meter round.

characters.appearance: man age 35, brown skin, tall forehead, short dark curls, compact beard, watchful eyes
characters.name: Ewan Evers
characters.intro: A dressing for my palm. Old filter came out all at once and I was still pulling.
characters.afterPurchase: My hand's all right. We put a handle on the next filter before we installed it.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have you got wound dressings for a tool bag?

characters.appearance: woman age 38, pale skin, long narrow face, dark braid around crown, calm gaze
characters.name: Ailsa Rill
characters.intro: Measuring glass for the inspection cart. The laboratory wants figures. 'About half a mug' didn't do.
characters.afterPurchase: Gave them the figures. They asked me to put them in mugs for the public notice.
characters.subsequentErrand: A cylinder for taking samples, please.

characters.appearance: man age 59, olive skin, graying ponytail, rugged cheeks, full salt-and-pepper beard
characters.name: Roland Keene
characters.intro: Float gauge is lying again. I want wire to hang a weight beside it.
characters.afterPurchase: Gauge was right. The old weight had hollowed out. Saved the new one as a check.
characters.subsequentErrand: I need some wire I can bend by hand.

characters.appearance: woman age 30, deep brown skin, shaved sides and swept curls, confident expression
characters.name: Josie Flint
characters.intro: There's a tap running down somebody's wallpaper. I've shut the main off. Now I need cloth and an understanding neighbour.
characters.afterPurchase: Wallpaper dried. The cat slept on my folded cloth for two days.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any fabric I can spare for a plumbing call?

characters.appearance: woman age 64, tan skin, narrow eyes, loose gray bun, visible age lines
characters.name: Edith Rowe
characters.intro: Got batteries? I keep my survey notes on a recorder. Today's notes consist of one long dying squeak.
characters.afterPurchase: Went back to the first junction and said it all again. Shorter version this time.
characters.subsequentErrand: Power for a recorder. It's a long pipe run.

characters.appearance: man age 46, pale skin, blond receding hair, sturdy jaw, clean shaven
characters.name: Nolan Merrick
characters.intro: I need an electronic spare for a fault board. The lamps all come on except the one marked FAULT.
characters.afterPurchase: Replaced the contact. Got a lovely bright fault light. Now for the actual fault.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying electronic parts for the maintenance board.

characters.appearance: woman age 42, olive skin, wide cheekbones, short plum-brown curls, small spectacles
characters.name: Tabitha Strand
characters.intro: I want a cylinder I can trust. My partner and I have the same gauge reading and different feet full of water.
characters.afterPurchase: Did the test on a tray. Partner's boots dried out on the heater while we worked.
characters.subsequentErrand: Measuring glass for a pressure test.

characters.appearance: man age 28, dark skin, broad jaw, flat top hair, friendly expression
characters.name: Kian Ames
characters.intro: Any inexpensive hand tools? I've two apprentices sharing one driver and it's making them both very polite and very slow.
characters.afterPurchase: They got through the whole practice panel. Then they started swapping tools again by choice.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm putting together a tool roll for a new apprentice.

characters.appearance: woman age 50, freckled tan skin, wavy chestnut hair with gray temples, steady eyes
characters.name: Corinne Calder
characters.intro: The incident book says nobody here has ever cut themselves. The bandage drawer says otherwise. Could you fill it?
characters.afterPurchase: Left a pencil in the drawer. Got three honest entries by teatime.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings for the safety cupboard. I count them out myself.

characters.appearance: woman age 36, warm brown skin, wide nose, dark coiled hair tied high, calm direct expression
characters.name: Maeve Stillwell
characters.intro: A magnifier. I want to see whether that little ridge is in the casting or in my glasses.
characters.afterPurchase: It's in the casting. Got my glasses cleaned anyway.
characters.subsequentErrand: Do you have a glass for checking machined parts?

characters.appearance: man age 52, tan skin, broad face, receding gray hair, trimmed mustache, tired gentle eyes
characters.name: Otis Ashford
characters.intro: Anything I can make at the dispatch desk? A water main burst at the exact moment I bit into my lunch yesterday.
characters.afterPurchase: Used a bowl with a lid. Ate it in four calls. Still counts as a meal.
characters.subsequentErrand: Noodles for the switchboard break.

characters.appearance: woman age 44, olive skin, angular nose, black bob with one silver streak, reserved expression
characters.name: Beryl Morrow
characters.intro: You sell a little torch? I need to read a number off the back of a pump. I can't get my head in there.
characters.afterPurchase: Six-eight-nine. We'd been ordering parts for six-eight-six since before I started there.
characters.subsequentErrand: Another torch for the drain crew. The other one lives in my pocket.

characters.appearance: man age 29, dark skin, narrow jaw, cropped curls, slight crooked smile
characters.name: Ronan Venn
characters.intro: Can I get water for a repair crew? Promised them a tap by noon. I've seen the hole. It won't be noon.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the tap back at three. Nobody had to go without in the meantime.
characters.subsequentErrand: Water to take out on call. We shut ours off before we start.

characters.appearance: woman age 61, pale skin, lined face, short white hair and rectangular spectacles
characters.name: Sybil Tallis
characters.intro: We're saying goodbye to the old shop steward today. He asked for coffee and absolutely no speeches.
characters.afterPurchase: Made him coffee. He gave the longest speech I've ever heard.
characters.subsequentErrand: Coffee for the workshop. There's a mug for visitors.

characters.appearance: woman age 32, dark brown skin, oval face, side braid and small scar at eyebrow
characters.name: Gwen Fenwick
characters.intro: Dressings, please. Steam through a pinhole looks like nothing till it catches your sleeve.
characters.afterPurchase: The sleeve was worse than my arm. Took it to the training room so the new crew can see.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm restocking the steam crew's first-aid kit.

characters.appearance: woman age 27, freckled light skin, red hair in loose bun, wide-set modest-sized eyes
characters.name: Alma Hale
characters.intro: Bandages. We've a man outside the clinic insisting he's fine. I'd like to put one in his hand before he leaves.
characters.afterPurchase: He came back for a clean one the next morning. Used his own name this time.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something for small wounds, please.

characters.appearance: woman age 55, dark skin, silver twists, round strong face, skeptical eyebrow
characters.name: Nadine Darrow
characters.intro: Have you got the plain shampoo? A woman on my ward asked if she could wash her hair before her son comes.
characters.afterPurchase: He came after supper. She'd been sitting up waiting for him with a towel round her shoulders.
characters.subsequentErrand: Same plain shampoo again, please. She liked it.

characters.appearance: man age 35, brown skin, tall forehead, short dark curls, compact beard, watchful eyes
characters.name: Micah Evers
characters.intro: I'm short a cylinder at the dispensary. The missing one's got a little flower growing in it.
characters.afterPurchase: Left the flower alone. There's a second shoot beside it now.
characters.subsequentErrand: Measuring glass, please. For its intended purpose.

characters.appearance: woman age 38, pale skin, long narrow face, dark braid around crown, calm gaze
characters.name: Irene Rill
characters.intro: The ambulance indicator thinks we're turning left all day. I could use an electronic part to trace the fault.
characters.afterPurchase: Loose relay. We can turn right again without getting waved at.
characters.subsequentErrand: Got any electronic spares for the garage?

characters.appearance: man age 59, olive skin, graying ponytail, rugged cheeks, full salt-and-pepper beard
characters.name: Conrad Keene
characters.intro: Small waters, please. The waiting room fountain's behind the triage desk and people are afraid to ask.
characters.afterPurchase: Put bottles out where they could reach. The little paper cups stopped disappearing too.
characters.subsequentErrand: Bottled water for the waiting room.

characters.appearance: woman age 30, deep brown skin, shaved sides and swept curls, confident expression
characters.name: Luz Flint
characters.intro: A proper dressing. A neighbour's been using strips off the same old pillowcase for a week.
characters.afterPurchase: Saw him this morning. Hands back in his pockets instead of behind his back. That's something.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings for the house calls.

characters.appearance: woman age 64, tan skin, narrow eyes, loose gray bun, visible age lines
characters.name: Moira Rowe
characters.intro: Battery for the clinic van lamp. Had to read a house number by knocking and asking what it was.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the next address first try. Lady said that hasn't happened in years.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any power cells? I've a night route.

characters.appearance: man age 46, pale skin, blond receding hair, sturdy jaw, clean shaven
characters.name: Ravi Merrick
characters.intro: Cheap cloth for a class. I'd rather let students make mistakes on sleeves than on people.
characters.afterPurchase: Spent the afternoon letting ten grown adults tie me to a chair. It's a sling class.
characters.subsequentErrand: Cloth for practice slings. Doesn't matter what colour.

characters.appearance: woman age 42, olive skin, wide cheekbones, short plum-brown curls, small spectacles
characters.name: Salma Strand
characters.intro: A little light for the dispensary window. We've two labels that look the same once the sun goes down.
characters.afterPurchase: Moved one shelf as well. Less chance of an error when I'm tired.
characters.subsequentErrand: Torch for the evening counter, please.

characters.appearance: man age 28, dark skin, broad jaw, flat top hair, friendly expression
characters.name: Theo Ames
characters.intro: I'm replacing the filter in a school sink. The children are watching. I've already been asked if I know how to do it.
characters.afterPurchase: The child who asked stayed to help. Held the old one the right way up, which is more than I did.
characters.subsequentErrand: A drinking-water filter for my rounds.

characters.appearance: woman age 50, freckled tan skin, wavy chestnut hair with gray temples, steady eyes
characters.name: Harriet Calder
characters.intro: Got something to eat in the van? Just sat through my break with a woman who wouldn't let go of my hand.
characters.afterPurchase: Her daughter came in. Same grip. I got five minutes to eat after that.
characters.subsequentErrand: Wrapped food, please. I don't always get a table.

characters.appearance: woman age 36, warm brown skin, wide nose, dark coiled hair tied high, calm direct expression
characters.name: Noor Stillwell
characters.intro: Looking for a screwdriver. There's a squeak in a man's new hand and he says it's ruining his card games.
characters.afterPurchase: One quarter turn. He can shuffle without announcing his cards now.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any small hand tools for the fitting bench?

characters.appearance: man age 52, tan skin, broad face, receding gray hair, trimmed mustache, tired gentle eyes
characters.name: Abel Ashford
characters.intro: Wound supplies. I've got to carry everything up three flights. Show me the little packs first.
characters.afterPurchase: A boy carried the bag up for me. Ten years ago I delivered him in that building.
characters.subsequentErrand: Small dressings for the upstairs clinic.

characters.appearance: woman age 44, olive skin, angular nose, black bob with one silver streak, reserved expression
characters.name: Leila Morrow
characters.intro: Coffee? I've an hour before the blood run. If I go home I'll sleep right through it.
characters.afterPurchase: Got the cooler there on time. Home by breakfast, bed by breakfast and a half.
characters.subsequentErrand: Something for the coffee pot at dispatch.

characters.appearance: man age 29, dark skin, narrow jaw, cropped curls, slight crooked smile
characters.name: Ilan Venn
characters.intro: Empty bottles. We're sorting the donation cupboard. An unlabelled bottle with something IN it is the last thing we need.
characters.afterPurchase: Finished the count. Half a crate of empties and a very nice button someone thought was medicine.
characters.subsequentErrand: Have you got clean empty glass?

characters.appearance: woman age 61, pale skin, lined face, short white hair and rectangular spectacles
characters.name: Ruth Tallis
characters.intro: Wire to mend a privacy screen. I can hear it falling over from my little room downstairs.
characters.afterPurchase: The screen held. So now I get called about the squeaky door. That's progress.
characters.subsequentErrand: Wire for small repairs at the clinic.

characters.appearance: woman age 32, dark brown skin, oval face, side braid and small scar at eyebrow
characters.name: Simone Fenwick
characters.intro: Fresh produce, please. I'm visiting a man who says he doesn't cook for one. I'm staying for supper.
characters.afterPurchase: He made us both supper. Packed my leftovers up in a jam jar.
characters.subsequentErrand: What produce looks good today? I make food when I visit.

characters.appearance: man age 67, pale weathered skin, broad nose, bald crown and gray side hair, deep smile lines
characters.name: Basil Brass
characters.intro: A power cell for the cycle timer. Somebody's been timing the sterilizer by a song with three different endings.
characters.afterPurchase: We timed the song for fun. Not one version was close.
characters.subsequentErrand: Battery for the clean-room kit.

characters.appearance: woman age 48, tawny skin, stocky build, dark auburn crop, practical serious expression
characters.name: Faiza Corven
characters.intro: I'll take dressings. We used the last of the small ones on a carpenter who kept apologising for the sawdust.
characters.afterPurchase: He came back with a little shelf for the first-aid box. Shed sawdust all over the hall again.
characters.subsequentErrand: Dressings, whatever size you've got.

characters.appearance: man age 41, olive skin, hooked nose, wavy black hair, light stubble, relaxed shoulders
characters.name: Hugo Lowell
characters.intro: Coffee for the recovery room. Some days nobody wants to talk. Gives us something to do with our hands.
characters.afterPurchase: One of the regulars made the pot himself. Stayed to wash the cups too.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying beans for the evening group.

characters.appearance: woman age 38, pale skin, long narrow face, dark braid around crown, calm gaze
characters.name: Mabli Rill
characters.intro: Let me see your seasoning. My stall's between a fishmonger and a soap seller. Can't trust my nose out there.
characters.afterPurchase: Tried it at home. My nose works. That's bad news for the soap seller.
characters.subsequentErrand: I'm buying seasoning by the bottle today.

characters.appearance: man age 59, olive skin, graying ponytail, rugged cheeks, full salt-and-pepper beard
characters.name: Cyril Keene
characters.intro: Soda for a sample tray. I want something the stallholders can actually afford to order.
characters.afterPurchase: The porter bought the first one. Everybody followed his lead. Next time I'm paying him for the tasting.
characters.subsequentErrand: Which sodas have you got in?

characters.appearance: woman age 30, deep brown skin, shaved sides and swept curls, confident expression
characters.name: Hana Flint
characters.intro: I'm buying hand tools. A man tried to sell me a driver with my dad's initials on it. Now I've a mind to finish Dad's set.
characters.afterPurchase: Found the old roll. You can see where the handles sat in it for years.
characters.subsequentErrand: Any hand tools with a bit of life left?

characters.appearance: woman age 64, tan skin, narrow eyes, loose gray bun, visible age lines
characters.name: Agatha Rowe
characters.intro: A water I can put in a side pocket. My big jug rode in somebody else's cart all the way to the locks.
characters.afterPurchase: Caught up with my jug. He'd put his name on it already.
characters.subsequentErrand: Need a bottle for the road.

characters.appearance: man age 46, pale skin, blond receding hair, sturdy jaw, clean shaven
characters.name: Bruno Merrick
characters.intro: I'm buying produce for a stallholder who's just had a baby. Says she can do the morning market. She can't.
characters.afterPurchase: She let me do two mornings. Third morning she was there with baby and scales.
characters.subsequentErrand: What fruit or veg have you got for the market?

characters.appearance: woman age 42, olive skin, wide cheekbones, short plum-brown curls, small spectacles
characters.name: Zelie Strand
characters.intro: I'm after a magnifier. The client wants the little mark on a cup authenticated and I'm afraid it's dried gravy.
characters.afterPurchase: It washed off. Family decided to keep the cup. Very sensible.
characters.subsequentErrand: A glass for looking at makers' marks.

characters.appearance: man age 28, dark skin, broad jaw, flat top hair, friendly expression
characters.name: Idris Ames
characters.intro: I'm trying coffee on the tea stall. Quiet trial. My landlord reads every new sign as an invitation to raise the rent.
characters.afterPurchase: Sold out quietly. Haven't put up a sign.
characters.subsequentErrand: Beans, please. You can leave the paper bag plain.

characters.appearance: woman age 50, freckled tan skin, wavy chestnut hair with gray temples, steady eyes
characters.name: Margot Calder
characters.intro: Empty bottles. I've got one space left in the blue crate and it's been bothering me all morning.
